transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-02
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Connor (Redwood); Sanjay Patel, Avery Ruiz, Morgan Li (Kestrel)

Summary (auto): quick discovery covering self-serve path, what free credits look like, how long to get to first token, and when Dedicated/Private makes sense for them.

[00:00] Maya: hi everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood - i'll kick off and Liam our solutions engineer is here as well
[00:08] Sanjay: hey Maya, thanks, yeah we have a short agenda - want to understand the free credits and how quickly our app team can actually make calls
[00:15] Maya: great, short answer is you can be generating tokens within an hour if you want to do the quickstart path, with SDKs and curl examples. we give credits that cover a small pilot, i'll send the link after the call
[00:28] Avery: can you clarify what the credits cover? are they only for hosted API or can we use them toward dedicated?
[00:36] Maya: primarily hosted for the PLG credits, dedicated is a separate purchase and has a different procurement flow, but we can talk about trials on dedicated if you need predictable throughput for the pilot
[00:48] Morgan: quick interjection - security is a must for us, we need SOC2, SSO, and KMS integration. also any e2e data residency stuff?
[00:58] Liam: yeah we support SOC2, SAML/SSO, and KMS/HSM integrations on Private and Dedicated. Hosted has tenant isolation and audit logs; for strict residency or customer-managed keys we usually recommend Private (VPC) or on-prem option
[01:13] Sanjay: what's the time to ship if we go hosted first then move to private? are there migration pains?
[01:20] Liam: typically customers go hosted to prove product-market-fit; migration to Dedicated/Private involves pinning model versions and transferring traffic. KV cache and session state need care but we have tooling to export prompts and caches. timeline varies but plan on 4-8 weeks for a changeover if you need custom network setup
[01:37] Avery: cost wise we care a lot — latency vs cost. our product has chat and codegen features at peak hours, how do we reason allocation?
[01:46] Maya: we surface cost per token and latency breakdowns in the console. for PLG you can start with lower-cost quantized models for responses and route high-value requests to higher-tier models or Dedicated pools for predictable latency
[01:58] [crosstalk, faint]
[02:04] Sanjay: do you have an SDK sample in node? we use node microservices
[02:09] Liam: yes, node and python SDKs. I'll paste a sample in slack/email. typical quickstart: create API key, run example curl or SDK call, you'll see the first token in under a minute depending on warmup
[02:21] Sanjay: warmup? do we need to warm containers?
[02:24] Liam: for cold-start there's a small latency hit, we do continuous batching and warm pools for hosted to mitigate that, but for strict SLOs Dedicated with reserved capacity is best
[02:36] Avery: what's the free credits amount roughly?
[02:39] Maya: it depends on program, but usually aligns to a couple hundred dollars worth of tokens which is enough for a small pilot. I'll share exact redeem link and expiration
[02:48] Morgan: any guardrails on data retention? We can't keep PII for more than X days
[02:53] Liam: we have configurable retention settings on Private and Dedicated and audit logs. hosted can also be configured to not persist user data on request - it's in the security pack which I'll send
[03:05] Sanjay: what about throughput - we expect a 200 rps burst for the feature flagged beta, is that feasible on hosted?
[03:13] Liam: depends on model and sequence length. hosted is multi-tenant so bursts are possible but not guaranteed; for guaranteed throughput you'd reserve capacity in Dedicated. we can design a small benchmark to mimic your workload
[03:25] Maya: maybe useful if we outline a pilot: 2 weeks on hosted using credits, instrument three endpoints for cost/latency, then decide on Dedicated if we need more SLAs.
[03:36] Avery: timeline-wise we want to ship an MVP in Q1. procurement and security will be involved though.
[03:41] Sanjay: procurement - we need standard legal terms and an exit plan, what does Redwood's procurement cadence look like?
[03:47] Maya: hosted is self-serve so you can start without legal; Dedicated/Private contracts are negotiated with enterprise terms. we have a standard master services agreement that most customers sign—I'll share a redlined copy and typical timelines
[03:57] Morgan: curious on quantization — will your hosted models use 4bit? we care about hallucinations too
[04:05] Liam: we offer a catalog of model variants, some quantized profiles that trade off quality for cost. we also provide eval hooks and prompt set regression alerts so you can detect quality drops after a model change
[04:19] Sanjay: ok would be helpful to see a small benchmark and cost estimate for our expected workload
[04:24] Maya: noted, Liam will put together the bench and cost math.
[04:28] [10:00 cut where Maya shares link? audio glitch for a few seconds]
[06:10] Liam: i'll include sample scripts to measure p95 latency and tokens per second, and show how to pin a model version and route traffic in the console
[06:22] Avery: how does the console surface per-route costs? we have multiple product routes that have different user counts
[06:27] Liam: console gives token-level cost and a breakdown by route, model, and token type (prompt vs completion). you can tag routes and get charts for each tag
[06:37] Sanjay: do you have SSO examples for GSuite and Okta?
[06:41] Maya: yes, SAML 2.0 with both. it's a standard setup for enterprise. 
[06:48] Morgan: network wise, if we do Private in our VPC, who manages subnets and peering?
[06:54] Liam: Customer manages their VPC and we provide deployment manifests; for on-prem we provide an appliance. For VPC peering we have runbooks and can walk infra through it.
[07:03] Sanjay: if we wanted to prove-hosted first, can we route only a small percentage of production traffic?
[07:09] Maya: yes, you can do canary traffic and A/B route using the rollout tools. start low then increase as you monitor costs and latency.
[07:18] Avery: what's your SLAs like on hosted?
[07:21] Maya: hosted is best-effort; we publish uptime metrics. Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. If SLA is a hard requirement for beta, Dedicated might be needed
[07:32] Sanjay: ok that helps. can you show me an example flow for sign-up to first call programmatically?
[07:37] Liam: sure: 1) sign up, 2) create API key, 3) install SDK, 4) run sample request - code snippet. I'll paste exact commands after. Expect to see tokens returned quickly, but for p95 we should run a few parallel requests to warm things up
[07:53] [transcription note: speaker labels may be imperfect here]
[08:01] Avery: do you have any references in healthcare? compliance is heavy for us
[08:07] Maya: yes, we have customers in regulated spaces. Private deployment + support for KMS and audit export tends to be the pattern. I'll include a short case study in the follow-up pack
[08:18] Sanjay: let's talk numbers at a high level - cost per 1k tokens on hosted vs dedicated reserved pricing?
[08:24] Maya: hosted public MSRP will be in the pricing doc; Dedicated pricing is custom but generally lower per-token if you commit. For short numbers, hosted might be X cents per 1k, Dedicated can be materially lower depending on commit size — I'll share ranges
[08:38] Morgan: we also run an internal concatenation service for logs — any advice on keeping prompts small?
[08:44] Liam: prefix caching and prompt templating are big wins. our Optimize product suggests batching/caching configs and quantization profiles to balance cost and quality
[08:54] Avery: what sort of logs and tracing do you provide? we need per-request traces to debug bad outputs
[09:00] Liam: per-request traces, token breakdown and model traces are available in Console, and you can send traces to external tracing systems via webhooks
[09:09] Sanjay: ok let's align on pilot success criteria - we're thinking: p95 < 600ms for typical chat, cost <$0.02 per user per month for base usage, and no PII retention beyond 30 days. is that reasonable?
[09:22] Maya: that's reasonable as starting targets for the pilot. we'll validate with the benchmark
[09:27] Avery: any blockers on our side to try self-serve now?
[09:31] Maya: no blockers, you can start. I recommend we set up the pilot and I'll send the redeem link so infra can provision keys and run the scripts
[09:39] Morgan: do you happen to have a sample legal redline? procurement will ask
[09:43] Maya: yes, I'll include a sample MSA and data processing addendum in the follow-up pack
[09:49] Sanjay: timeline—if we start this month, can we be shipping MVP in Q1?
[09:54] Maya: yes, that's within reach if pilot goes well and procurement moves at typical speed.
[09:59] [short silence]
[10:05] Liam: i'll also recommend a tiny validation test: 1k concurrent simulated users over 5-minute window to measure behavior. we'll provide scripts and the expected metrics to collect
[10:18] Avery: perfect. one more question: do you support tool calling or function calling from the model output?
[10:24] Liam: yes, we support function-calling patterns and structured output. that's included in the API and SDKs
[10:30] Sanjay: ok thanks - anything else?
[10:33] Maya: recap of next steps: I'll send credits and quickstart, Liam will draft benchmark plan, Sanjay will send sample workload. We'll reconvene after Kestrel runs the pilot or in two weeks to sync
[10:45] Sanjay: sounds good, thanks everyone
[10:47] Avery: thanks
[10:48] Morgan: thanks

End of transcript. Some timestamps approximate; audio had a short dropout around 00:10-00:12 and again at 04:28.
